title: Dispute decisions are published and recorded in the Atlas itself, turning resolutions into standing precedent
content:
A.2.8.1.1.2.3.4 requires that the Core Facilitator "publishes the decision on the Sky Forum and updates the Dispute Resolutions Active Data document in the Atlas, redacting any confidential information as needed." A.2.8.1.2 makes that document Active Data with the Core Facilitator as Responsible Party under a Direct Edit protocol.

Writing outcomes into the Atlas rather than only onto a forum thread has a consequence beyond record-keeping. The Atlas is the ecosystem's rule set, so resolutions live alongside the rules they interpret and become findable by anyone reading the relevant provision. Over time this builds an interpretive layer — how ambiguous Accord terms have actually been read — without amending any rule.

That matters because Ecosystem Accords are bilateral agreements between Primes, invisible in their negotiation but enforceable by Sky Governance. Published decisions let a third Prime drafting its own Accord see how a similar term was resolved, which is the practical mechanism by which private contracts converge on shared conventions.

The redaction clause is the concession: commercial disputes contain figures and strategies the parties will not want public, so the published decision is the reasoning with the sensitive detail removed. Precedent value survives; verifiability partially does not.

The record is currently thin — A.2.8.1.2.0.6.1 lists a single entry, the September 2025 Grove/Spark dispute over the effective date of their Accord. Notably the first dispute between the ecosystem's two flagship Primes was about *when their agreement started*, which is a useful signal about where Accord drafting most needs precision.
description: The Core Facilitator posts the decision on the Sky Forum and updates the Dispute Resolutions Active Data document, redacting confidential material, so outcomes accumulate as a citable record.
